title: Release build must explicitly clear MLFLOW_SKINNY so an ambient value cannot produce mlflow-skinny
answers: release build produced mlflow-skinny instead of mlflow
full mlflow wheel built as skinny when MLFLOW_SKINNY is set in the environment
legacy 2.11 setup.py chooses the wrong package name
how do I make dev/build.py build the full mlflow package regardless of env vars
body:
Symptom: the release workflow's `--package-type release` run publishes a skinny package (mlflow-skinny) when the CI or shell environment has MLFLOW_SKINNY set.
Root cause: dev/build.py:build starts from `{**os.environ, **extra_env}`, so any ambient MLFLOW_SKINNY leaks into the release build, and the legacy setup.py selects mlflow-skinny whenever `bool(os.environ.get("MLFLOW_SKINNY"))` is true.
Fix pattern: every package-type branch in dev/build.py:main passes the package-selecting variable explicitly (`{"MLFLOW_SKINNY": ""}` for release, `{"MLFLOW_SKINNY": "1"}` for skinny), so the child process never inherits a stale value.
Constraints: applies to the legacy single-setup.py layout on branch-2.11. An empty string is falsey under the setup.py check; a new package-selecting env var must get the same explicit treatment in both branches.
applies: branch-2.11 legacy single-setup.py packaging only; v3+ branches have their own dev/build.py.
says: The release pipeline published a lightweight package instead of the full platform package.
Our production release build produced the slim package rather than standard installation.
Why did the full package release publish missing dependencies like the slim variant?
Ensure the official release artifact builds the complete package despite inherited environment settings.
The automated release run created the lightweight distribution instead of the full wheel.
search: Release packaging in dev/build.py:main must explicitly pass MLFLOW_SKINNY as an empty string for release and 1 for skinny packages so builds do not inherit ambient environment variables. This applies strictly to branch-2.11 legacy single-setup.py packaging, where setup.py selects mlflow-skinny whenever MLFLOW_SKINNY evaluates to true. Any new package-selecting environment variable must receive identical explicit assignment in both package-type branches.
